searchText: You can actually use `Union[null, FieldType]` to represent `Optional` But it looks more like a workaround TBH Unions are not too well supported among SSZ implementations, and are not currently used anywhere across core Ethereum <@881905303011086387> why is the SSZ format unaffected? if we serialize `LightClientUpdate` per https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/blob/master/apis/beacon/light_client/updates.yaml#L37 which will contain `LightClientHeader` separate question, how commonly is the SSZ response used over JSON? When the entire object is fixed-size, SSZ will simply send each field in sequence. As for `hash_tree_root()`, because the extra container only has a single item, there is no extra tree layers being generated, so root is the same. SSZ is the only format used on libp2p, and is also recommended on REST in any situation, as the response size is much smaller. the JSON format is used when easy access from JavaScript is needed, and for developers to better investigate issues. On REST, you can select SSZ format with a HTTP `Accept` header Note that for the `/events` stream, only JSON is supported due to limitation with HTTP Server sent events At least for Nimbus, `/events` encoding was bugged until yesterday, so I doubt anyone was using that one yet ah makes sense, after the change the object is still the same on the wire good to know re: SSZ benefits in REST thanks! Exactly. SSZ doesn't encode the structure itself, just the content JSON is very poor for compressing all those sha256 hashes. it sends them as a hex string on the wire, needing 2 characters for each byte of data BTW: For the light server you will also need the two topics here: https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/blob/master/apis/eventstream/index.yaml And sorry for the noise with the `beacon` wrapper while you are implementing it. Hope it's not too painful thanks I must have missed these. when are they consumed? no worries, should be easy to change 🙂 just an alternative to polling. e.g., a wallet could use this endpoint to stay up to date w.r.t. latest header also useful in case you don't want to miss intermediate headers

excerpts.author: mynervini
excerpts.content: separate question, how commonly is the SSZ response used over JSON?

excerpts.author: etan_status
excerpts.content:
When the entire object is fixed-size, SSZ will simply send each field in sequence.
As for `hash_tree_root()`, because the extra container only has a single item, there is no extra tree layers being generated, so root is the same.

excerpts.author: etan_status
excerpts.content:
SSZ is the only format used on libp2p, and is also recommended on REST in any situation, as the response size is much smaller.
the JSON format is used when easy access from JavaScript is needed, and for developers to better investigate issues.
On REST, you can select SSZ format with a HTTP `Accept` header

excerpts.author: etan_status
excerpts.content: Note that for the `/events` stream, only JSON is supported due to limitation with HTTP Server sent events

excerpts.author: etan_status
excerpts.content: At least for Nimbus, `/events` encoding was bugged until yesterday, so I doubt anyone was using that one yet

excerpts.author: mynervini
excerpts.content:
ah makes sense, after the change the object is still the same on the wire
good to know re: SSZ benefits in REST
thanks!

excerpts.author: etan_status
excerpts.content: Exactly. SSZ doesn't encode the structure itself, just the content

excerpts.author: etan_status
excerpts.content: JSON is very poor for compressing all those sha256 hashes. it sends them as a hex string on the wire, needing 2 characters for each byte of data
